Oxigraph Static Pipeline & Search Requirements

How the IRIS catalogue is compiled into named graphs with Oxigraph, checked, published, and queried. How to build and query it is in the iris-oxigraph skill.

[!IMPORTANT] Binary assets are never embedded in the graph. PDFs, image bitstreams and covers stay on the CDN. The graph holds typed entities, Dublin Core values, containment, and each bitstream's file name, media type, byte size and copyright verdict.

1. Pipeline Architecture & Placement

The pipeline is modelled in the cat-harness BPMN process files, which are the source of truth:

  • Package and distribute partitioned N-Quads (spine, community partitions, manifest, prepared queries): processes/kg/nquads-distribution.bpmn

  • Run a prepared SPARQL query in Oxigraph (browser WASM or local engine): processes/kg/named-query-execution.bpmn

How this instance feeds the pipeline from IRIS and publishes to Cloudflare is in IRIS CDN Exporter: processes; its nightly full rebuild calls nquads-distribution.

2. Pipeline Integration Stages

Stage 1: Build-Time Ingestion, Skolemization & 2-Tier Partitioning

  • Input, either:
    • catalogue/nodes/*.json (communities, collections, items, bitstreams) and site/dublin-core/*.dc.jsonld (Qualified Dublin Core records conforming to dublin-core.ts); or
    • --records <dir>: DSpace records exported by scripts/iris-cdn/run.ts.
  • Tool: scripts/build-iris-oxigraph.ts (--out <dir>, default dist/oxigraph/).
  • Actions:
    1. Skolemization: mint deterministic URIs (https://iris.who.int/entity/item/{handle}#{prop}_{idx}) for every anonymous compound Dublin Core object. The build fails if any blank node (_:) remains.
    2. Partitioning:
      • Tier 1 (Spine): <https://iris.who.int/graph/spine> — hierarchy, item Handles, title, first creator, issued date, and bitstream descriptors with copyright verdicts. who-iris-spine.nq and .nq.gz.
      • Tier 2 (Partitions): <https://iris.who.int/graph/community/{id}> — the full Dublin Core of each community's items (MeSH authorities, abstracts, spatial tags, govdoc, ISBN). iris_who_int_graph_community_{id}.nq and .nq.gz.
      • Catalogue and metadata graphs: iris_who_int_graph_catalogue.nq(.gz) and iris_who_int_graph_metadata.nq(.gz), merged in who-iris-dataset.nq and .nq.gz.
    3. Manifest & prepared queries: subgraph-manifest.json (partition registry) and queries.json (prepared SPARQL).
    4. Every file is sorted and de-duplicated, so unchanged partitions are byte-identical across rebuilds.

Stage 2: Build-Time Tests

bun run scripts/build-iris-oxigraph.ts
bun test scripts/tests/iris-oxigraph.test.ts

The test builds the dataset and checks: zero blank nodes; multi-condition search, date-range search and facet counts; additive community mounting; the discoverySearch prepared query; that the manifest's partition files exist; and that a rebuild over exported records leaves unchanged partitions byte-identical.

Not yet checked by any test: every item declares a collection and community path; every bitstream declares bytes and media type; every item has a 10665/... Handle.

Stage 3: CDN Distribution

Exported data is published to Cloudflare: R2 behind the Cloudflare CDN, with release history in a git repository on Cloudflare Artifacts (see IRIS CDN Exporter: deployment).

  • scripts/iris-cdn/run.ts rebuilds the dataset over the exported records and lists each output file in the release manifest as graph/<file>:
    • who-iris-spine.nq.gz (Tier 1 spine)
    • subgraph-manifest.json (partition registry)
    • iris_who_int_graph_community_{id}.nq.gz (Tier 2 partitions)
    • who-iris-dataset.nq.gz (merged graph)
    • queries.json (prepared queries)
  • The bytes are stored in R2 under sha256/<aa>/<digest>.
  • Cache Policy: Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable on sha256/*. A changed file has a new digest, so a cached object never goes stale.

Stage 4: Client-Side Execution (Browser WASM)

The intended client pattern (no page in this repository loads Oxigraph yet; the replica's home page filters an index embedded in the page with plain JavaScript):

  1. Create an in-memory store: const store = new oxigraph.Store();
  2. Fetch the spine (who-iris-spine.nq.gz) and subgraph-manifest.json.
  3. Decompress and load: store.load(decompressedNq, { format: 'application/n-quads' }).
  4. Run prepared SPARQL locally for title search, year filters and open-access gates.
  5. When the user selects a community, fetch its .nq.gz partition from the manifest and store.load() it; existing quads are kept.

3. Formal Requirements (Checkable Specifications)

ID Requirement Verification Method
SR-1 No Binary Embeddings in Graph: No RDF literal or URI may represent raw file bytes (base64 or blob data). Bitstreams are nodes reached by dspace:hasBitstream, with fileName, fileBytes (integer) and mediaType. Not automated.
SR-2 Upstream Skolemization at the Extractor (Zero Blank Nodes): Extractors and ingestion pipelines assign deterministic URIs (https://iris.who.int/entity/item/{handle}#{prop}_{idx}) at extraction for all compound nodes (creators, subjects, dates). No blank node (_:) may be emitted. The build throws on any residual blank node; iris-oxigraph.test.ts asserts none in the dataset.
SR-3 Multi-Graph Isolation: Catalogue containment and rights gates reside in <https://iris.who.int/graph/catalogue>; bibliographic records in <https://iris.who.int/graph/metadata>. Not automated. The catalogue graph also carries rdf:type, rdfs:label and dcterms:title.
SR-4 Sub-50ms Query Execution: Standard discovery and complex search queries over the materialized dataset complete in under 50 milliseconds in WASM. Not measured by any test.
SR-5 Additive Subgraph Mounting: store.load() of an additional named subgraph must not clobber, mutate, or duplicate loaded quads. iris-oxigraph.test.ts: a query before mounting returns N items; after mounting a community, N + M.
SR-6 Handle Authority: Every item subject URI uses the Handle system: https://hdl.handle.net/10665/{id}. Graph check: every a dspace:Item subject starts with https://hdl.handle.net/.
SR-7 Compressed Transport Ceiling: At full scale (300,000 items), a community partition must not exceed 25 MB compressed. Not measured in CI.
SR-8 Prepared Query Equivalence: Every entry in queries.json is valid SPARQL 1.1 and runs against the dataset with 0 errors. iris-oxigraph.test.ts runs discoverySearch only.
SR-9 Append-Only Streaming Partitioning: The build writes partitions as an append-only stream, with memory bounded regardless of corpus size (300,000 items). Not met: buildIrisDataset holds and sorts every quad in memory; StreamingPartitionWriter is unused. Target: heap under 250 MB for the whole corpus.

4. Scale Modeling & Corpus Sizing (300,000 Items)

WHO IRIS holds 273,559 items across 1,057,223 files, about 361.55 GiB of PDFs, reports and images (see iris-dspace §Scale). The figures below are estimates for about 300,000 items.

Sizing Comparison: Raw Full-Text vs. Pure KG Extract in Oxigraph

Metric Raw Full-Text in Oxigraph Pure KG Metadata Extract (Architecture Standard)
Content Included Full OCR extracted page text + bibliographic metadata Dublin Core, MeSH authorities, bitstream descriptors, access gates, hierarchy paths
Binary Blobs in RDF 0 (strictly excluded) 0 (strictly excluded)
Quads / Triples ~45,000,000 quads (including sentence/paragraph chunks) ~12,000,000 quads (~40 quads per item)
Uncompressed N-Quads ~45 – 60 GB ~1.2 – 1.5 GB
Brotli / Gzip Payload ~8 – 12 GB compressed ~95 – 140 MB compressed (>90% compression ratio)
Partition Size (per Community) ~1.2 – 1.8 GB compressed ~12 – 20 MB compressed
WASM In-Memory RAM > 4 GB (Exceeds 32-bit WASM limit → Browser Crash) ~35 – 65 MB RAM per loaded partition
Load Time over CDN (4G/Fiber) Impossible in browser 150 ms – 350 ms
Query Latency Slow regex/filter scans (> 5,000 ms) < 15 ms index-backed graph pattern matching

Architectural Recommendation

  1. Never load full text into Oxigraph. Substring filters over millions of text literals are slow and exceed browser memory.
  2. Hybrid search:
    • A static inverted index (e.g. Pagefind, MiniSearch, or a sharded SQLite FTS5 WASM slice) handles full-text lookup and yields candidate item IRIs.
    • The candidates go into Oxigraph as VALUES ?item { ... } for facets, MeSH hierarchies, collection constraints and copyright gates.

5. Registered Tools, Skills & Verification

Executable Scripts & Tools

  • scripts/build-iris-oxigraph.ts: N-Quads compiler, skolemizer and gzip writer.
  • scripts/iris-oxigraph-search.ts: IrisOxigraphEngine — boolean search, facet counts and incremental subgraph mounting.
  • scripts/gen-iris-pages.ts: static site generator; the home page's facet chips and filters run over an index embedded in the page, not Oxigraph.

Test Suites

  • Unit: bun test scripts/tests/iris-oxigraph.test.ts.
  • End-to-end: bunx playwright test cat-harness-tools/test/who-iris-search.e2e.ts (browser search, facet chips, open-access filters, multilingual UI).

Formal Skills & Specifications

  • skills/iris-oxigraph.md: requirements OX-1 through OX-9.
  • docs/oxigraph-pipeline-requirements.md: system requirements SR-1 through SR-9.
